title: LGBTQ+
mv: And even as they did not like to retain God in their knowledge, God gave them over to a debased mind, to do those things which are not fitting.
mvp: “And even as they did not like to retain God in their knowledge, God gave them over to a debased mind, to do those things which are not fitting.” Romans 1:28 (NKJV)
assignment: Write out five (5) attitudes Christians should have toward people who struggle with sin (2x5=10marks).

b.x: LGBTQ+ is an inclusive term used to describe a diverse community of people with different sexual orientations and gender identities who do not identify as exclusively heterosexual or cisgender. The acronym stands for Lesbian, Gay, Bisexual, Transgender, Queer or Questioning, with the plus (+) representing other sexual orientations, gender identities, and expressions.
L - Lesbian: A lesbian is a woman who is emotionally, romantically, or sexually attracted to other women.

G - Gay: This typically refers to a man who is emotionally, romantically, or sexually attracted to other men. However, it can also be used as a general term for people attracted to the same gender, including women.
B - Bisexual: This person is emotionally, romantically, or sexually attracted to both the male and female genders.
T - Transgender: This is someone whose gender identity differs from his or her birth sex. For example, someone whose natal sex is male but now identifies as female is a transgender woman.
Q - Queer or Questioning: This refers to individuals who are exploring or unsure about their sexual orientation or gender identity.
+ (Plus): The plus (+) symbol represents all other identities not specifically covered by the five main letters. This includes but is not limited to:

i: Intersex - People born with both male and female reproductive organs. This is also called hermaphroditism in humans.
Asexual - People who experience little or no sexual attraction to others.
Pansexual - People who are attracted to others regardless of gender.
Non-binary - People whose gender identity does not fit within the traditional categories of male or female, etc.

b.x: The Bible specifically address same-sex sexual acts, without labels like "LGBTQ+" (a modern term). For instance, Leviticus 18:22 and 20:13 warn men against the detestable act of having sexual relations with a man as one does with a woman. Romans 1:26-27 describes both male and female same-sex acts as against nature. 1 Corinthians 6:9-11 lists “men who have sex with men” among other sins. 1Timothy 1:9-11 mentions homosexual acts among behaviours contrary to sound doctrine.

Members of the LGBTQ+ community clamour for acceptance, protection and inclusivity in various spheres of society, including the Church. Unfortunately, the Bible says God gives them over to their passions and “to do those things which are not convenient; unbecoming, indecorous, shameful” (Romans 1:26-28). This means their hearts are allowed to be hardened by their sins, like the case of Pharaoh (Exodus 4:21). As a result, they can no longer see the error of what they are doing (Proverbs 10:17; Hebrews 3:7-10). Without an awareness of their sinfulness, there will be no repentance (2 Corinthians 4:3-4). Without repentance, there will be no forgiveness (Acts 8:22). Without forgiveness, there is no salvation (2 Corinthians 7:10; Romans 10:10).

Therefore, the fact that someone is a member of the LGBTQ+ community does not mean that we cannot love (agape) them (Leviticus 19:18; Romans 13:8). Believers should pray for the salvation of their souls the same way they would any other person in sin (1 John 5:16-17). They should be treated with the same dignity as they would anyone else (Romans 13:7). However, this does not mean that Christians should approve of their sin or compromise with them (Ephesians 5:11).
The gender orientation and sexual behaviour of the members of the LGBTQ+ community contradict God’s plan for humanity. Yet, God does not want anyone to perish.
